notes: 16 turns. The stretch begins exactly on Avelín's bold label, so it does not open mid-utterance. LABELS: the president's label is printed four different ways in these seven paragraphs and I kept each as rendered rather than normalising. 'Sr. Presidente (López Arias).-- ' and 'Sr. Presidente (López Arias).-- ' both render 'Sr. Presidente (López Arias).--' (the space before the parenthesis is inside the bold run in the first, outside it in the second); 'Sr. Presidente (López Arias).\n--' renders with a space, 'Sr. Presidente (López Arias). --'. The holder is outside the bold run every time. Alfonsín's one-word turn ('Sí.') is printed 'Sr. Alfonsín.-- ', with the stop and dash OUTSIDE the bold run and no space before the stop, unlike his other three turns ('Sr. Alfonsín. --'). That short turn and 'Pido la palabra.' are exactly the kind that get dropped, so I flag them. CONTINUATIONS I DID NOT COUNT: after 'Vamos a escucharlo después.' a separate unlabelled paragraph reads 'Tiene la palabra el señor senador Pichetto.' — still the president's same turn. Likewise Alfonsín's second turn runs over three paragraphs, Pichetto's over three, Losada's over two, and the president's last turn continues into 'Se va a votar en general.' ITALICS THAT ARE NOT AN EVENT: inside Alfonsín's speech the Latin tag 'omni definitio in jure periculosa est' is set in italics. It is spoken (he introduces it with 'permítanme un latinazgo'), so it is part of his turn, not a stenographer's note. The two real notes are the voting lines at the end. No headings, no back-links, no inserted document in this stretch. UNSURE: nothing that changes the turn count. The only judgement call was the Latin italics, decided against calling it an event because the sentence around it announces it as speech.
